name: Congenital Myopathy with Internal Nuclei and Atypical Cores
aliases: CM with Internal Nuclei and Atypical Cores
Congenital Core Myopathy with Internal Nuclei

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Myopathy with Internal Nuclei and Atypical Cores

criteria.description: Muscle biopsy showing internalized nuclei and presence of atypical cores
Congenital or early-onset hypotonia and muscle weakness predominantly affecting proximal muscles
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with congenital myopathies (e.g., ACTA1, RYR1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic muscle biopsy findings plus clinical presentation of congenital hypotonia and weakness; genetic confirmation supportive but not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic heterogeneity exists; muscle biopsy remains the diagnostic cornerstone.

searchTerms: muscle cells with nuclei located inside fibers
abnormal placement of muscle cell nuclei

pathognomonic.symptomName: Atypical core lesions in muscle fibers
searchTerms: unusual core-like areas in muscle fibers
muscle fibers with abnormal core lesions

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital hypotonia with proximal muscle weakness
searchTerms: low muscle tone and weakness near the trunk from birth
congenital floppy muscles with proximal weakness
weakness of muscles close to body center present at birth
weakness in facial muscles including droopy eyelids
drooping eyelids and weak facial muscles

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective muscle involvement with fatty infiltration
Chest X-ray may show restrictive lung disease features
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating internal nuclei and atypical core structures

distinguishingFeatures: Classic central cores on muscle biopsy without prominent internal nuclei
Presence of nemaline rods on muscle biopsy
Distinct clinical phenotype with facial weakness and hypotonia
Predominance of centralized nuclei without atypical cores
Different genetic mutations such as MTM1, DNM2

redFlags: Severe feeding difficulties leading to failure to thrive
Early onset severe hypotonia with respiratory distress
references: Jungbluth H, et al. Congenital myopathies: clinical features and diagnosis. Nat Rev Neurol. 2018.
North KN, et al. Congenital myopathies: pathology and molecular genetics. Neuromuscul Disord. 2014.
